description: The FD FORMAT clause (records written to the file are formatted to an external representation suitable for presentation or printing, and converted back on input), ISO/IEC 1989:2002 13.16.22 and 2023 13.18.24 - a COBOL-2002 introduction (FORMAT is a 2002 reserved word per 8.9; at COBOL-85 it is a user-defined word). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 sequential file description entry's clauses are BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS, LINAGE and CODE-SET (§1985:VII.3.2.2; §1985:VII.3.2.1: 'The file description entry furnishes information concerning the physical structure, identification, and record-names pertaining to a sequential file'); §2002:13.16.22 introduces the clause: 'The FORMAT clause specifies that records written to the file are to be formatted to an external representation during the output process and records read from the file are to be converted from the external format into internal representation during the input process', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 57: 'For sequentially-organized files, the FORMAT clause provides the capability to present data so that people may read it.' §2014:13.18.24 carries the 2002 sentence unchanged, so 2014 = 2023. kb/Work PB5578.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. FMT9CL.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
FILE-CONTROL.
    SELECT F1 ASSIGN TO "fmt9cl.dat".
DATA DIVISION.
FILE SECTION.
FD F1 RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 1 TO 20 CHARACTERS
    FORMAT CHARACTER DATA.
01 R1.
    05 R1-NUM PIC S9(4).
    05 R1-TXT PIC X(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    STOP RUN.
